command: llvm-mc -triple=x86_64 -filetype=obj research/evidence/experiments/EXP-0047/fixture.asm -o out.o && llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text out.o out.bin
notes: Eighteen 8/16-bit mov memory instructions on the 0.18.0 extension windows. Instructions 1-7 are the four word -base-ext rows: r8/r9/r10/r11/r13/r14/r15 bases, both disp8 ends (127, -128) and both disp32 promotions (128, -129). Instructions 8-13 are the REX-less low-byte -base-ext rows, the same bases and displacement widths. Instructions 14-18 are the widened template-40 rows: instruction 14 keeps base 0 (rax) as the counterexample that a low base still encodes with REX.B = 0 and the same four bytes as 0.17.0, while 15-18 use r8, r9 and r15 in both directions at both displacement widths. Every base is a high register except instruction 14; %rsp and %r12 are deferred (ADR-0045) and measured in probes.txt. `input_sha256` is fixture.asm (the source above); `output_sha256` is the 100-byte .text.
